schema_version: v0 — component-charter shape; migrates into the intention envelope when MAP.md Q6 lands
what: The ONE path to EVERY inference host, and the compile-once gate every inference request passes through. Since 2026-08-08 (ruling the-inference-proxy-is-a-rules-stack) the path is a RULES STACK: three authored stacks beside the code (stacks/providers.json — costs, connection handling, enabled+why; stacks/models.json — names, parameters, pros/cons, scores; stacks/combos.json — the routable provider/model pairings) plus route.py, a nest of sieves (the second carrier of cairn.tools.base.nest) that lets out the lowest-cost route — and the lowest cost answer is NEVER 127.0.0.1. The machine half (this LAN's endpoints, API keys) lives in ~/.cairn/devices/inference_domain/0/hosts.json, instance-space — moved there 2026-08-17 on Akien's ruling ('devices/inference_domain/0/ is exactly right. ruled with a smile'), and resolved through cairn.tools.base.address rather than spelled. host.py's `ollama_resolver` built WITHOUT an endpoint routes: shake the nest, dial survivors cheapest-first (usually Hex), walk to the next rung on HostUnreachable only, refuse loudly when the walk exhausts; an explicit endpoint pins one host (the proofs' seam and the walk's own inner rungs). An inference request is a TICKET (a workflow node); the domain runs that ticket's workflow inside the owner: RECEIVE -> CANONICALIZE -> lookup -> (hit) VERIFY -> ANSWER, or (miss) METER -> RESOLVE -> RECORD -> ANSWER. Primitives (cairn/devices/inference_domain/domain.py): `canonicalize(request)` — reduce a request to its canonical form (first cut: structural, sorted-key JSON); `resolve(request, resolver=...)` — run the whole workflow and return {answer, hit, canonical, cost, provenance} (cost/provenance ride back ADDITIVELY since 2026-07-29, ticket a-node-holds-one-claim: the host's real counters had ALWAYS been recorded in the row and never returned, so a caller could not ask what a call actually cost and the embed ceiling stayed folklore — on a hit these are the STORED values unchanged, the spend avoided and the served_from marker); `yield_report()` — the meter read back (tokens SPENT on misses vs AVOIDED by hits). The cache is one db_domain-owned, append-only table `inference_calls` (owner `inference_domain`) that is BOTH the compiled answers (verdict='miss' rows carry the resolved answer + its falsifier/horizon/provenance/cost) and the meter (every call lands a row).
why: Telos 1 — demonstrate inference compilation. An answered question must become structure (Law 1): the second time a canonically-identical request arrives, the host is NOT touched — a stored answer is verified (its horizon still holds, T1.3) and served, and that untouched host call IS compilation happening. The domain being the SOLE pipe (Law 6 + Law 4: one owner, reached only through its gate, no other door — the same move as db_domain's sole path to 5432 and the tester's owned network seal) is exactly what makes metering free and complete (T1.2: there is no uninstrumented path to the host), so the saving is a measured fact, not a hope (Law 3). Append-only, on purpose (Law 7): the cache is a log, never mutated — a stale answer is out-voted by verification, not overwritten, which is why db_domain's INSERT-only primitives suffice.
invoke: import: `from cairn.devices.inference_domain import domain`. Prove: `python3 cairn/devices/inference_domain/proofs/test_inference_domain.py` (exit 0 = green), or under the tester via `TesterDevice().run_proof(...)`. Needs db_domain's one-time provisioning (an OS-named LOGIN CREATEDB role); the cache is a db_domain-owned table.
node_class: device (domain) — a spine device by role (the sole path to the inference host). Today it is workflow primitives + the cache; the BaseDevice introspection FACE and bus-fronting are a thin runtime wrapper, a filed edge below.
entry: FRESH design, standard mechanism. The design — the sole-owner gate a third time, the inference request AS a ticket whose states are its workflow, the compile-once cache that verifies before it serves, append-only so the store never mutates a record of truth — is Cairn's, converged with Akien 2026-07-21 (the conversation that corrected 'enforcer' to 'gated ownership' and 'features' to 'workflow states'). The mechanism is ordinary: sorted-key JSON canonicalization + db_domain's owner-gated store; nothing crossed as carried code. The real host client is a LATER wiring (instance-space credentials, a real endpoint), exactly as db_domain filed its live FORWARD path.
state_and_history: compiled to state.json (projected window) + history.json (append-only voyage) beside this charter — the charter-state-history split; this file stays pure intention+why, the operational voyage lives in the sidecars (Law 1/4/7)
filed_edges: (a) CANONICALIZE is structural only (sorted-key JSON) — it does NOT collapse SEMANTIC equivalence (paraphrases/equivalent prompts); that is T1.3's hard core, wants a /challenge pass + Akien's read before a shape is committed

(b) CLOSED 2026-08-08 and replaced by its residues: the host client lives HERE, wired to real hosts through the rules stack (edge closed as filed — 'when a second appears this reads from ~/.cairn/'). Residues: the gemini transport does not exist yet (a gemini-protocol survivor is walked past loudly, never dialed ollama-shaped — grows the day Akien lands the key); the ollama-cloud and gemini rungs are listed and loudly refusing until their keys land in ~/.cairn/devices/inference_domain/0/hosts.json (Akien's act); gemini's model-mapping rule (local tags do not name gemini models) is the open edge its combo row carries; authored costs in providers.json are a labeled Law-3 hypothesis until the meter measures them
(c) VERIFY checks the HORIZON only; the stored FALSIFIER is carried for T1.4 active invalidation (evaluating it, and propagating a falsifier upstream, is a later edge)
(d) the BaseDevice FACE + bus-fronting (callers poke the domain over the bus rather than importing it) are the runtime face, deferred until a prober/runtime pulls them, as db_domain deferred its face
gates: proof gate — proofs/test_inference_domain.py, run by the tester. Durability gate: not done until proven AND committed.
falsifier: RED on any of: (1) a canonically-identical repeat touches the host (the resolver is called a second time) — compile-once breached, the whole thesis; (2) a request past its horizon is served from the cache (blind replay — verify-before-answer breached, T1.3); (3) a hit returns anything but the stored answer byte-for-byte (a record of truth mangled on the way out — Law 7); (4) a non-owner write to the cache table SUCCEEDS (Law 6 breached); (5) a call does not land a meter row, or yield_report miscounts SPENT vs AVOIDED (the meter is incomplete — Law 3, T1.2); (6) any module OTHER than inference_domain opens the inference host (sole-path breached). ENFORCED as of 2026-08-06 by cairn/tools/import_sieve over the WHOLE tree at proof time, and as of 2026-08-08 at BUILD time too — build_inspector's sole_path_holds sieve runs the same mesh on every inspection (ruling item 1: 'THAT NEEDS TO BE IN THE BUILD INSPECTION'). Residue: a subprocess curl imports nothing and is not seen; (7) a generate miss lands with provenance.host = 127.0.0.1 while a ruled provider answers — the ruled NEVER crossed live (watched by probes/does_the_route_leave_loopback.py); (8) the stacks exist but a route is decided by a literal anyway — rules decorative. Wrong-shape signal: if metering/caching turn out to need to live INSIDE the resolver loop rather than at this domain boundary, 'the domain' was the wrong seam.
how_it_learns: Directly, and it is the first device whose learning is its point. The meter IS the learning surface: `yield_report` turns each call into evidence — tokens AVOIDED climbing against tokens SPENT is the measured answer to 'is inference compilation paying off?' (Telos 1, Law 3). Its own horizon: today it learns WHETHER the cache pays (the yield); it does not yet learn WHICH questions are the same (semantic canonicalization, T1.3) or WHEN an answer has gone wrong (active falsifier invalidation, T1.4) — those are the two named edges where the learning deepens as real inference traffic pulls them. The librarian above it (the next spine steps) is the first heavy consumer that will pull them.
traces_to: Telos 1 (demonstrate inference compilation — T1.1 answers-as-structure, T1.2 every call metered because this is the sole pipe, T1.3 a hit verifies before it answers, T1.4 falsifier+horizon on every answer)
Law 6 (exactly one owner; reached only through the owner's gate — the sole path to the host)
Law 4 (physics over policy — sole path was by construction, and became physics 2026-08-06 via cairn/tools/import_sieve; gates not supervisors)
Law 7 (append-only cache — a record of truth is never mutated)
Law 3 (the meter makes the saving measured; a stored answer carries its own expiry)
Law 1 (an answered question becomes structure, not a re-derivation)

gated_by_why: THE HANDS THIS INTENTION'S OWNER-GATE ADMITS — the machine-readable half of `owner` above, and the only half cairn.devices.harbor_master.clearance.clear() reads. Compared by EXACT LIST MEMBERSHIP, never by scanning (the prose is what a human reads; this list is what a gate can stand on). DERIVED FROM `owner`, NOT INVENTED, and filled 2026-08-15 at the moment a real crossing needed it: the chat-verb voyage's PROVED crossing was refused by the clearance gate naming this exact field, this charter's path, and the one-line fix. The derivation is measured against the corpus rather than argued: this charter's owner prose ('CC owns inference_domain's code + proofs and gates writes to them. Akien owns the design ratification ... and the node-class definitions') is near word-for-word harbor_master's, and harbor_master and build_inspector — the two charters whose prose splits the same way, CC gating WRITES and Akien owning the DESIGN — both derive ['CC']. The charters that derive ['Akien','CC'] say something different (tools/base: 'Akien owns the words, ratification is his gate'). So the split is not about seniority and this list is not a ranking: RATIFICATION IS NOT A CROSSING. Akien outranks every artifact here including this file, and nothing in this list touches that — what he owns at this address is whether the design is right, which he settles by ruling, not by moving a boat through a gate. A hand that is not a member does not become one by naming itself (Law 6's second clause); standing comes through a grant minted by a member, or through an edit to this list, which is itself an owner-gated write to this charter.
proof: proofs/test_inference_domain.py — compile-once (a repeat does not touch the host); canonical equivalence (key order is the same question); verify-before-answer (a stale entry re-resolves); the answer is served unchanged (Law 7); the owner gates the cache (Law 6); the meter measures spent against avoided (Law 3). Run by the tester on a real db_domain store; self-cleaning (an ephemeral table, dropped). proofs/test_host.py — the host seam meters real counters or refuses, and the repo-wide sole-path mesh. proofs/test_route.py — the stacks carry the ruled rows by content, loopback is cut categorically (even as the last rung standing), unkeyed rungs refuse loudly, the walk fails over on unreachability only. proofs/test_watch_probe.py — the loopback watch judges fixture rows. Green: `python3 cairn/devices/inference_domain/proofs/<each>.py`.
provenance: Born 2026-07-21 as the next step of the code spine after the heartbeat+bus+system-device block, in a design conversation with Akien that reframed the device twice before a line was written: an inference request is a TICKET whose workflow-states are the device's insides (not a bag of features), and the 'enforcer' that makes those states physics is not a supervisor but a gated resource only one owner reaches (the db_domain pattern, a third time).
